title: Kepler transit survey from dedicated instrument to population-scale exoplanet observability and K2 recovery
pressure: Known exoplanets were sparse and detection methods were biased; estimating the prevalence and size distribution of planets required long-duration, high-precision, repeated stellar photometry.
preExistingWorldModel: Transit detection was understood, but no dedicated space survey had continuously monitored a sufficiently large stellar field with the required precision and duration.
candidateRoutes: repurpose remaining hardware with solar-pressure-balanced K2 pointing
observationsAndInstruments: Kepler launched in 2009 as a dedicated transit survey and accumulated thousands of planet candidates.
Loss of a second reaction wheel in May 2013 ended the original pointing mode.
Engineers used solar radiation pressure as a virtual stabilizing element and NASA approved the K2 reformulation in May 2014.
decisiveTests: photometric precision and duration sufficient to detect repeated transits
population-level planet occurrence inferred from a well-characterized survey
whether degraded spacecraft could attain a new stable pointing regime
technicalOrScientificTransition: A purpose-built instrument converted a previously sparse discovery domain into population measurement; later recovery converted a failed pointing architecture into a different but scientifically useful mission.
rivalsAndFailures: Reaction-wheel failure invalidated the original observation mode.
K2 did not restore the exact original mission; it created a different observation programme under new physical constraints.
diffusionAndScaling: The survey shifted exoplanet science from individual discoveries toward a census of planet types and prevalence.
standardsAndInstitutions: NASA mission teams, proposal review and external follow-up scientists jointly maintained the evidence chain.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Candidate detection, confirmation and population inference remain different evidential standings.
secondOrderEffects: New observability changed the scientific question from whether exoplanets exist to their distribution and diversity.
sourceNativeSummary: Kepler is both an instrumentation-leverage case and a recovery case: the instrument changed the measurable problem space, while K2 shows that useful continuation can preserve purpose without pretending physical identity of the original mode.
